conventions.convention: Beta-sets are finite subsets of nonnegative integers. P({h₁>…>hₘ}) has parts hᵢ−m+i, with trailing zeros deleted. The l-shift adds l to each existing bead and adjoins 0,…,l−1. Abacus position ae+i lies on runner i, with row numbers increasing downward.

For finite e≥2, the core is obtained by top-packing each runner. The ordered quotient is computed only from a beta-set whose cardinality is divisible by e; its components are ordered by runners 0,…,e−1. Weight is the sum of their sizes.
Removing a node hook means deleting its corresponding rim border strip, rather than deleting its arm-and-leg node set.
The q-Schur core classification is stated in the stable range d≥n, over an arbitrary field with invertible q and quantum characteristic e. For e=∞, C∞(λ)=λ and the algebra is semisimple.

The Schur images use Murphy cell modules with restricted simple labels. Ordinary Dipper–James Specht modules are obtained by conjugating partition labels and applying the same θ pullback to every compared module; their nonzero simple labels are regular.
The Jantzen sum is the sum of positive filtration submodule classes, not successive quotient classes or merely the radical class. Equal-degree beta transfers are balanced and carry the sorting sign.

load_bearing.statement: Let F be a field, q∈F× have quantum characteristic e, n≥0 and d≥n. For partitions λ,μ of n with at most d parts, the Weyl modules Wλ and Wμ of SF(d,n) lie in the same block if and only if λ and μ have the same e-core. For e=∞, C∞(λ)=λ and the algebra is semisimple.

For e≥2 and a beta-set X of a partition λ, its node hooks correspond bijectively to pairs (b,g) with b∈X, g∉X and 0≤g<b, with hook length b−g. Removing the corresponding rim strip replaces b by g. The length is divisible by e exactly when b and g lie on the same runner.

For e≥2 and λ a partition, P(X(e)) is independent of the beta-set X of λ and is the common terminal partition of every maximal sequence of removable rim e-strip removals. It is an e-core. Any two normalized beta-sets give the same ordered quotient and weight.

Let F be a field, q∈F×, d,n≥1 and S=S(d,n). If a finite-dimensional right S-module M has all composition factors in a single block B and [M]=Σλ aλ[Wλ] with integer coefficients, then Wλ lies in B whenever aλ≠0.

For e≥2 and a partition λ, there is a bijection f from its hooks of e-divisible length to the hooks of Qe(λ), satisfying |H|=e|f(H)| and Qe(λ∖H)=Qe(λ)∖f(H), with removal interpreted as deletion of the corresponding rim strip.

For e≥2 and λ a partition of n, n=|Ce(λ)|+ewe(λ). Every maximal sequence of rim e-strip removals has exactly we(λ) steps, and we(λ)=|Qe(λ)| is also the number of node hooks of λ whose lengths are divisible by e.

Let F be a field and q∈F× have quantum characteristic e. For partitions λ,μ of n, the ordinary Dipper–James Specht modules Sλ,Sμ of HF,q(Sn) lie in the same block if and only if Ce(λ)=Ce(μ). For e=∞ the Hecke algebra is semisimple and each partition indexes its own block.

Over the fixed splitting field k of characteristic p>0, for n≥0 two group Specht modules Sλk,Sμk lie in the same block of k[Sn] if and only if their labels have the same p-core. Blocks are indexed by pairs (γ,w) with γ a p-core, w≥0 and n=|γ|+pw.

concerns.concern: The final prose says, “the invariant that separates them is the runner distribution of the beads,” although the displayed beta-sets have different cardinalities. Raw runner counts are not core invariants without fixing a common beta-set length: at e=3, (3) and (1,1,1) have the same empty core, but their canonical beta-sets {3} and {3,2,1} have counts (1,0,0) and (1,1,1). The computed counterexample is correct; the concluding wording needs the common-length qualification or reference to the recovered packed-core partition.

alerts.finding: The Given paragraph attributes “the charged beta conventions of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]” to that supplier. The cited definition uses finite subsets of nonnegative integers and defines no charge or infinite beta-set. This consumer instead introduces B={λᵢ+c−i:i≥1} locally in F1. Its local extension is explained, so this is a citation-attribution issue rather than a demonstrated failure of the mathematical result.

seams_checked.note: Read the relevant cellular, q-Schur, virtual-symbol, quantum-characteristic, Jantzen, Schur-functor and specialization suppliers before their consumers. The consumers retain stable rank, right-module conventions, balanced transfers, accumulated coefficients, filtration-submodule sums and the conjugate/θ dictionary. The unweighted semistandard normalization agrees with [Mathas, Corollary 4.12 and (4.13)](https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~bigelow/books/mathas.pdf); the corrected connectivity route agrees with [Lyle–Mathas, Proposition 3.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0607451).

Read the branching page and searched every listed item for assigned supplier IDs. The requirement is background only: no listed branching item directly cites an assigned core/block item, and the page does not restate a core/block proposition more strongly.

The fixed-component-core lemma faithfully uses the finite-e Hecke block iff, core independence and size formula, with the ordinary/Murphy translation explicit. The charged-height lemma correctly uses core-removal independence but misattributes charged infinite beta-set conventions to the finite beta-set definition; the presentation alert records this mismatch.
